title: Mutations: writes, callbacks and the cache
objectives: Write a custom hook around `useMutation` that owns the `mutationFn` and the cache follow-up, and block a double submit with `isPending`
Choose `mutate` or `mutateAsync`, and handle the rejection that `mutateAsync` throws
Predict when hook-level and call-level `onSuccess`/`onError`/`onSettled` run: their order, after an unmount, and for consecutive `mutate` calls
Keep a mutation pending until its invalidation has refetched, by returning the promise from a hook-level callback

sources.title: TanStack Query v5 docs: Invalidations from Mutations
TanStack Query v5 docs: Network Mode
TanStack Query docs: Migrating to TanStack Query v5

questions.prompt: `useMutation({ mutationFn: createTodo })` POSTs successfully, but the todo list on the same screen keeps showing the old rows. Why?

options.text: A mutation has no link to any query; nothing told the cache that the list changed
The mutation needs a `mutationKey` equal to the list's query key, so the library knows what to refresh
The list's `staleTime` is too long; with `staleTime: 0` it would refetch after the write
The mutation is still retrying in the background, so the list is waiting for it

questions.explanation: Queries are keyed; mutations aren't tied to any of them. A `mutationKey` identifies the *mutation* (for defaults, `useMutationState`, `isMutating`) — it never refreshes queries. Staleness only matters when a trigger fires, and a mutation isn't one. And mutations don't retry by default. Invalidate the affected keys (or write the response with `setQueryData`) in the mutation's `onSuccess`.

questions.prompt: A user double-clicks **Save**, which calls `addTodo.mutate(draft)`. Nothing else guards it. What happens?

options.text: Two POSTs go out and two todos are created; disable the button while `isPending`
One POST: identical `mutate` calls are deduplicated, like queries with the same key
One POST: `mutate` is ignored while the mutation is already pending
Two POSTs, but the first is cancelled, so only one todo is created

questions.explanation: Mutations run in parallel by default — no deduping, no queue, no cancellation. Each `mutate` is a new write. Disable the trigger while `isPending`, or give the mutation a `scope` so calls run one at a time (they'd still both run).

questions.prompt: `<button onClick={() => save.mutateAsync(draft)}>` — and the save fails. What happens?

options.text: `save.error` is set, and the promise nobody handles becomes an unhandled rejection
`save.error` is set and nothing else happens: `mutateAsync` catches its own rejection, like `mutate`
The nearest error boundary catches it and renders its fallback
The click handler throws synchronously and React logs the error

questions.explanation: `mutateAsync` returns a promise that rejects on failure; `mutate` is the variant that catches for you. The hook's state updates either way, so the UI can show `save.error` — but the dropped promise is also reported as an unhandled rejection. Error boundaries catch errors thrown while rendering, not rejections in event handlers. Use `mutate` here, or `await` inside `try/catch`.

questions.prompt: A dialog calls `save.mutate(draft, { onSuccess: () => queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: todoKeys.all }) })` and then immediately `onClose()`, which unmounts it. The save succeeds. What happens to the list behind the dialog?

options.text: It stays stale: callbacks passed to `mutate` don't run once their component has unmounted
It refreshes: the mutation still finishes, so every callback passed to it still runs
It refreshes when the dialog is next opened, when the callback finally runs
React warns about a state update on an unmounted component and nothing runs

questions.explanation: The docs are explicit: call-level callbacks "won't run if your component unmounts *before* the mutation finishes". Hook-level callbacks still run — the mutation lives in the `MutationCache`, not in the component. That's why cache follow-up belongs in the hook; keep call-level callbacks for UI the component owns. (React 18 also removed the unmounted-update warning.)

questions.prompt: `for (const t of ['A', 'B', 'C']) addTodo.mutate(t, { onSuccess: (todo) => toast(todo.title) })`, where `useAddTodo` also has a hook-level `onSuccess`. All three saves succeed. How often does each callback run?

options.text: The hook's: 3 times. The `mutate` one: once, for `'C'`
Both run 3 times
Both run once — only the last `mutate` call is sent
The hook's: 3 times. The `mutate` one: once, for whichever save finished first

questions.explanation: All three requests are sent, and the hook-level callback runs for each. But each `mutate` re-subscribes the hook's observer to the newest mutation, so callbacks passed to `mutate` fire once, for the last call — `'C'` — regardless of which response arrives last. Per-item effects belong at the hook level, or in `await Promise.all(items.map((t) => addTodo.mutateAsync(t)))`.

questions.prompt: `onSuccess: () => { queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: todoKeys.lists() }); }` — the Save button is `disabled={isPending}`. What does the user see after a successful POST?

options.text: The button re-enables while the list still shows the old rows
The button stays disabled until the list has refetched, because `onSuccess` is awaited
The list never refetches, because an invalidation that isn't awaited is dropped
The button stays disabled forever, because the dropped promise never settles the mutation

questions.explanation: The invalidation still runs — it just isn't returned, so the mutation doesn't wait for it and becomes `success` as soon as the POST resolves. Returning the promise (`onSuccess: () => queryClient.invalidateQueries(...)`, no braces) keeps `isPending` true until the refetch settles, so the user can't act on a list that doesn't show their todo yet.

questions.prompt: A successful `addTodo.mutate(t, { onSuccess, onSettled })` on a hook that defines `onSuccess` and `onSettled` too. In what order do the four run?

options.text: hook `onSuccess` → hook `onSettled` → call `onSuccess` → call `onSettled`
hook `onSuccess` → call `onSuccess` → hook `onSettled` → call `onSettled`
call `onSuccess` → call `onSettled` → hook `onSuccess` → hook `onSettled`
All four at once; the order isn't defined

questions.explanation: The hook's callbacks are part of the mutation itself — each is awaited, then the next runs — and the mutation settles after its `onSettled`. Only then does the observer notify the `mutate` call's callbacks. (Checked against v5.104; the error path is the same shape with `onError`.) So by the time a call-level callback runs, a returned invalidation from the hook has already finished.

questions.prompt: A mutation's endpoint answers 500. With default options, how many times does `mutationFn` run?

options.text: Once — mutations don't retry unless you set `retry`
4 — the first attempt plus 3 retries, like queries
3 — `retry: 3` means three attempts in total
Until it succeeds, with exponential backoff

questions.explanation: Mutations default to `retry: 0`; it's queries that retry 3 times on the client. Repeating a write is only safe when the endpoint is idempotent, so opt in deliberately (`retry: 3`). A mutation started *offline* is different: it isn't attempted at all — it waits, paused, and runs on reconnect.

prompts.prompt: The hook refreshes every list after a save, and stays pending until the refetch is done.
prompts.explanation: `useQueryClient()` reads the client from `QueryClientProvider`. Returning the invalidation's promise makes the mutation await it, so `isPending` covers the refetch too. (Since v5.89 the callback's fourth argument also carries the client: `context.client`.)

prompts.prompt: Clear the input only after a successful save, and block a second submit while one is running.
prompts.explanation: A call-level `onSuccess` is this form's own reaction: it runs after the hook's callbacks, and only while the form is mounted. `isPending` is true from `mutate` until the hook's last callback settles, which is exactly the window a second click must not start another POST.

prompts.explanation: `mutateAsync` resolves with the mutation's data, so the next step can use it, and rejects on failure — which makes the `catch` mandatory. `mutate` would return nothing to await.

snippets.question: In what order are the five lines logged?
snippets.answer: hook onMutate, hook onSuccess, hook onSettled, call onSuccess, call onSettled
snippets.explanation: `onMutate` runs before the `mutationFn`. The hook-level callbacks run inside the mutation, one after another; once the mutation has settled, the observer runs the callbacks you passed to `mutate`. (Logged in exactly this order headlessly against v5.104.)

code: mutationFn: (title) => api.createTodo(title), // "Todo 1" is the slowest to answer
// All three succeed; Todo 2 answers first, then Todo 3, then Todo 1.
snippets.question: What are `hookLog` and `callLog` at the end?
acceptable: hook: Todo 2, Todo 3, Todo 1 — call: Todo 3 only
snippets.explanation: Three requests run in parallel and the hook-level callback fires for each, in the order the responses arrive. Each `mutate` re-subscribes the observer to the newest mutation, so the call-level callback fires only for the last *call* — "Todo 3" — even though "Todo 1" finished last. (Run headlessly against v5.104.)

code: const list = useQuery({ queryKey: ["todos"], queryFn: fetchTodos }); // takes ~500 ms
// After save.mutate(…) succeeds, the list refetch is under way:
snippets.question: What's logged while the list is refetching? And with `return` added before `queryClient`?
acceptable: success / fetching, then pending / fetching with return
snippets.explanation: Without the return, the invalidation starts but nothing waits for it, so the mutation is `success` while the list is still fetching — a Save button keyed on `isPending` re-enables early. Returned, the promise is awaited inside the mutation, and it stays `pending` until the refetch settles. (Both orders were observed headlessly against v5.104.)
